Indian tennis star Sania Mirza has made history by becoming the first female player from the country to win a women's doubles Grand Slam title. 

Mirza, partnering with Swiss veteran Martina Hingis, clinched the Wimbledon women's doubles title in a thrilling final against Russian duo Ekaterina Makarova and Elena Vesnina. The Indo-Swiss pair won the match 5-7, 7-6, 7-5 in a contest that lasted over two hours.

The victory marks a significant milestone in Indian tennis, with Mirza becoming the first Indian woman to win a Grand Slam event. The 28-year-old from Hyderabad has previously won three mixed doubles Grand Slam titles, but this is her first in the women's doubles category.

Mirza and Hingis, who only started playing together earlier this year, have quickly become a formidable pair on the international circuit. They have won three titles in a row, including the Wimbledon crown, and have a 12-match winning streak.

The Indian tennis star, who turned professional in 2003, has been a trailblazer for women's tennis in India. She was the first Indian woman to win a WTA tour title and to break into the top 50 in the singles rankings.

Mirza's historic win has been widely celebrated in India, with Prime Minister Narendra Modi leading the tributes. "Well played @MirzaSania & @mhingis. You played wonderful tennis and registered a fantastic win at Wimbledon. We are proud and happy," he tweeted.

The All India Tennis Association (AITA) also lauded Mirza's achievement. "It's a very proud moment for us. Sania's victory will inspire many young girls in India to take up the sport," said AITA Secretary General Hironmoy Chatterjee.

Mirza's victory is not just a personal triumph but a significant moment for Indian tennis. It is hoped that her success will inspire a new generation of players and help to raise the profile of the sport in a country where cricket dominates.
